correctness.rationale: Coverage with pencil sizes 4+4+5=13 forces disjoint pencils and forbids a center-joining arrangement line. Every triple point uses one line from each pencil, so the 16 distinct intersections of the first two pencils must all be covered by the third. If the centers were collinear, put them at infinity; the third parallel pencil would cover a 4-by-4 grid with at most five values of x−λy. A real-linear projection injective on the two summand sets gives at least 4+4−1 distinct sum values (walk through the ordered first set with the least second element, then through the ordered second set with the greatest first element). This contradicts five. For triangular coordinates the quotients B/A lie in C. Each third-pencil line has one center plus eight off-center crossings counted with multiplicity, reduced by one per triple, so its singular-point count is 9−t(c). The six-point bound gives t(c)≥3 and forces quotient support exactly C of size five, with frequencies 4,3,3,3,3. The finite stabilizer of B/A has order dividing five; Kneser's theorem rules out order one since four plus four minus one is seven. Hence the stabilizer is μ₅ and both coordinate sets are four-element subsets of μ₅ cosets. Scale the missing element in each coset to one; their ratios are then μ₅. For this normal form the 16 grid points are triples; the remaining off-center incidences are 8 doubles (one on each first/second pencil line), and the pencil centers have counts 4,4,5. The linewise counts are 6 on the first eight lines, and 5,6,6,6,6 on the third pencil. Dimca–Pokora's exact propositions provide both linewise hypotheses for the lower-r member of the counterexample pair. They transfer by lattice isomorphism, so projective equivalence contradicts the required difference in r (and in ν).
residual_risks: The finite-field checker gives examples only; the characteristic-zero proof and independent incidence count do not rely on executing it. No rigidity claim is made without the two extra hypotheses, for other numerical types, or over arbitrary fields.

evidence: Marchesi–Vallès give existence of a roots-of-unity arrangement with the same combinatorics, and classical freeness criteria for deletions (including absence of all three sides). Dimca–Ibadula–Măcinic give a classification involving (3,4)-nets on 12 lines with double and triple points.
Kneser gives the general finite multiplicative-set lower bound via the stabilizer.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The roots-of-unity existence statement does not imply that every realization is projectively equivalent, and non-freeness for unequal inner-pencil sizes after all three sides are deleted does not equate ν or r in the generalized conjecture. A (3,4)-net does not cover this unequal three-pencil arrangement. Kneser applies only after identifying and bounding the quotient set; the small difference-set theorem alone does not classify these arrangements.

evidence: The counterexample setup and exact case require differing r and ν. The propositions give the two transferable line restrictions, not projective rigidity. The triangular results supply representative existence and classical freeness information. Kneser supplies the cardinality bound for multiplicative subsets.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior statements do not, by specialization alone, give the exclusion. The decisive additional implications are that the centers are noncollinear and that all five directions are used by the triple grid, making the quotient set of size five. Its stabilizer then fixes the projective class for every realization, not just existence of an example.

evidence: The equation is a two-line deletion of the 15-line Fermat arrangement without coordinate sides. Marchesi–Vallès use the same triangular description and multiplicative equations for inner triple points in §3 (Eq. (3.1)).

originality.rationale: The open numerical case, linewise constraints and monomial/triangular arrangement framework are prior. The distinct claim is projective uniqueness for every complex realization satisfying the two constraints, and thus exclusion of the numerical type from the cited generalized-Terao counterexample regime. The strongest checked triangular theorem gives a same-combinatorics roots-of-unity representative, not uniqueness; its noncomplete-triangle theorem concerns classical freeness, not equality of ν or r. Searches and comparisons are bounded.
residual_risks: An uninspected catalogue of deleted monomial arrangements or a broader exact realization-space theorem might cover this type. No priority is asserted for the normal-form equation itself or for the known triangular representation.

value.rationale: This is a complete projective classification on a numerical type explicitly left open by a generalized-Terao reduction, and it rules out that type regardless of which admissible lattice is considered. The connection between saturated triple grids and multiplicative small-set structure explains why the moduli collapse rather than merely supplying an example. The incidence constraints are derived in the target application, not arbitrary parameters chosen after observing uniqueness.
residual_risks: Only this one numerical type is eliminated, and a projective classification without the two linewise restrictions is not claimed.
